name: Goalkeeper
desc: A balanced goalkeeper in possession: distributes safely according to the team instructions.
tip: A solid base when the keeper is not good with his feet; pairs with Goal Kicks "Mixed".

name: Ball-Playing Goalkeeper
desc: Takes an active part in the build-up, takes risks passing and can come off his line to offer support.
tip: Essential with "Play Through Press". Without Passing/Composure ≥ 12 he is a source of dangerous turnovers.
moveNote: comes off his line to support the build-up

name: No-Nonsense Goalkeeper
desc: Plays it safe: clears, goes long, avoids risks in the build-up.
tip: A good partner for "Bypass Press" and Goal Kicks "Long" with a Target Forward.

name: Goalkeeper
desc: Standard defensive behaviour: alternates between staying on the line and coming out depending on the situation.
tip: A safe choice with a medium defensive line.

name: Line-Holding Keeper
desc: Stays on the goal line and reacts. Good for teams defending the box in a low block.
tip: Works best with a low defensive line; with a high line it leaves huge space in behind.
moveNote: stays on the goal line

name: Sweeper Keeper
desc: Comes off his line to sweep balls in behind the defence.
tip: A must with a high defensive line. Needs Anticipation, Decisions and Rushing Out.
moveNote: positions himself high to sweep balls in behind

name: Centre-Back
desc: Holds position in the build-up, simple passes to a midfielder or full-back.
tip: The "default" that never compromises the rest-defence.

name: Ball-Playing Centre-Back
desc: Holds position but is expressive on the ball: looks for progressive passes and switches of play.
tip: A BPD + a simple CB is the most stable pairing. Two BPDs only with a safe defensive midfielder.

name: No-Nonsense Centre-Back
desc: Careful: clears without hesitation, takes no risks in the build-up.
tip: Contradicts "Play Through Press". Use in a low block / direct play.

name: Advanced Centre-Back
desc: Steps into midfield (the defensive-midfield zone) in possession, creating a central overload.
tip: Make sure of cover: with an ACB, leave 2 centre-backs/IFB behind or a Half Back.
moveNote: steps into midfield

name: Overlapping Centre-Back
desc: Wide centre-back in a back 3 who overlaps down the flank in the final third.
tip: Only makes sense in a back 3. Needs stamina and a wing-back who comes inside so they do not get in each other’s way.
moveNote: overlaps down the flank like a wing-back

name: Centre-Back
desc: Defends on the line with balanced behaviour: steps out to the ball carrier when it makes sense.
tip: The base choice; adjust with his partner’s role (one steps out, the other covers).

name: Covering Centre-Back
desc: Cautious: stays slightly behind the line to cover depth.
tip: The classic partner of a Stopping Centre-Back. Ideal with a high line and a quick centre-back.
moveNote: stays behind the line covering depth

name: Stopping Centre-Back
desc: Aggressive: steps out of the line to press the player between the lines.
tip: Excellent against an attacking midfielder/false 9. Needs a Covering partner.
moveNote: steps out of the line to squeeze between the lines

name: Covering Wide Centre-Back
desc: Wide centre-back (back 3) who defends reactively and deeper, covering the channel.
tip: Protect the back of a very attacking wing-back.
moveNote: covers the channel, deeper

name: Stopping Wide Centre-Back
desc: Wide centre-back (back 3) who steps out aggressively to press in the half-spaces and channel.
tip: Very good against opposing AMCL/AMCR. More freedom than in a back 4.
moveNote: steps out aggressively into the half-space

name: Full-Back
desc: Holds position and width; supports without bombing forward constantly.
tip: Safe. Pair with a winger who comes inside to keep the width.

name: Inside Full-Back
desc: Tucks inside and becomes a third centre-back in possession (back 3 in the build-up).
tip: Great for rest-defence. The other side can have an attacking full-back.
moveNote: tucks in as a third centre-back

name: Wing-Back
desc: Pushes on to give width and cross; appears a lot in the final third.
tip: Needs high Stamina. Pair with an Inside Forward/Inside Winger ahead.
moveNote: pushes up the flank and gives width

name: Inside Wing-Back
desc: Holds position and moves inside (into the defensive-midfield zone) in possession.
tip: Creates a 3-2 in the build-up. Needs a winger giving width on the same side.
moveNote: moves inside, alongside the defensive midfielder

name: Playmaking Wing-Back
desc: Comes inside and takes over the creating from deep. Expressive.
tip: One per side/tactic at most. Take creative responsibility away from the DLP if you use both.
moveNote: moves inside and organises

name: Advanced Wing-Back
desc: Goes even further forward, almost like a winger. Considered one of the strongest roles in FM26.
tip: Leaves the flank exposed: compensate with a Covering Wide CB / Wide Covering CM.
moveNote: goes all the way to the byline, almost like a winger

name: Full-Back
desc: Standard flank defending, holds the line.
tip: A balanced base.

name: Holding Full-Back
desc: Stays deeper and narrower to protect the centre-back against direct attacks; joins in late.
tip: Good with the opposite side pressing high (asymmetric structure).
moveNote: stays deep and narrow protecting the centre-back

name: Pressing Full-Back
desc: Steps out aggressively to the opposing wingers high up the pitch.
tip: Pairs with Pressing Trap "Outside". Leaves space in behind — needs Acceleration.
moveNote: pushes up to press the winger

name: Wing-Back
desc: Drops back to form a back 5 when needed.
tip: The base for a back 3.

name: Holding Wing-Back
desc: Cautious: holds position in a back 5.
tip: Low block 5-4-1 / 5-3-2.
moveNote: holds the back 5

name: Pressing Wing-Back
desc: Pushes up to press the opposing full-back/winger.
tip: Ideal in a pressing 3-4-3.
moveNote: pushes up to press

name: Defensive Midfielder
desc: Holds position in front of the defence; circulates the ball carefully.
tip: The anchor of the rest-defence. Almost every tactic has at least one of these "safe" players.

name: Deep-Lying Playmaker
desc: Holds position and is the main organiser from deep. Expressive.
tip: Needs passing lanes: pair with an IWB or BPD. Avoid with "Bypass Press".
moveNote: stays back to distribute

name: Half Back
desc: Drops between the centre-backs in the build-up, forming a back 3.
tip: Lets both full-backs push on. Redundant with an IFB on the same side.
moveNote: drops between the centre-backs (back 3)

name: Box-To-Box Midfielder
desc: Pushes up into the attacking-midfield zone and arrives in the box.
tip: Stamina and Work Rate are non-negotiable.
moveNote: arrives in the box as a second wave

name: Box-To-Box Playmaker
desc: Pushes into the attacking-midfield zone as a creator.
tip: Good in a double pivot with a safe DM.
moveNote: pushes up to create between the lines

name: Defensive Midfielder
desc: Standard defensive behaviour in front of the defence.
tip: The base option.

name: Dropping Defensive Midfielder
desc: Drops into the centre-back line out of possession (back 5).
tip: Low block against 2 strikers.
moveNote: drops into the defensive line

name: Screening Defensive Midfielder
desc: Cautious: closes central passing lanes and refuses to be dragged out.
tip: Protects zone 14.
moveNote: closes central passing lanes

name: Wide Covering Defensive Midfielder
desc: Moves across to cover the flank when the full-back pushes on.
tip: The natural partner of a very attacking wing-back.
moveNote: moves across to cover the flank

name: Pressing Defensive Midfielder
desc: Steps out to press high from the defensive-midfield position.
tip: Gegenpress. Leave another midfielder covering.
moveNote: steps out to press from defensive midfield

name: Central Midfielder
desc: Balanced: supports the build-up and joins the attack in moderation.
tip: The glue that balances the midfield.

name: Midfield Playmaker
desc: Midfield organiser, expressive, demands the ball.
tip: A single central creator per tactic is usually enough.

name: Wide Central Midfielder
desc: Moves out to the flank (the former Mezzala/Carrilero in possession), giving width from midfield.
tip: Perfect with a winger who comes inside or an IWB.
moveNote: moves out to the flank from midfield

name: Channel Midfielder
desc: Attacks the channels between centre-back and full-back — a discreet game-breaker.
tip: Pairs with a false 9 who frees up space.
moveNote: attacks the channel between centre-back and full-back

name: Advanced Playmaker
desc: Looks for space between the lines to create.
tip: Needs runners ahead of him (IF, CF, Channel Fwd).
moveNote: looks for space between the lines

name: Attacking Midfielder
desc: Occupies the space between the lines and threatens goal (the old attacking CM at MC).
tip: Great for arriving in the box as a second wave.
moveNote: occupies zone 14 and threatens from distance

name: Central Midfielder
desc: Standard midfield defending.
tip: The base option.

name: Pressing Central Midfielder
desc: Pushes up to press (can form the first line with the striker).
tip: Gegenpress / high block.
moveNote: pushes up to press

name: Screening Central Midfielder
desc: Holds position, blocks central passing lanes, presses less.
tip: Compact mid/low block.
moveNote: protects the central zone

name: Wide Covering Central Midfielder
desc: Covers his own flank (the former Carrilero) when the full-back/wing-back has pushed on.
tip: The Advanced Wing-Back’s partner.
moveNote: covers the full-back’s flank

name: Wide Midfielder
desc: Holds position and width, a balancing role.
tip: Classic 4-4-2.

name: Winger
desc: Stays wide, goes to the byline and crosses.
tip: Pair with targets in the box (CF, TF, Poacher).
moveNote: goes to the byline to cross

name: Inside Winger
desc: Comes inside as a creative threat.
tip: The full-back on the same side should give width (WB/AWB).
moveNote: moves into the half-space to create

name: Playmaking Winger
desc: Starts wide, comes inside, very expressive.
tip: One creator per flank at most.
moveNote: starts wide and comes inside to organise

name: Wide Midfielder
desc: Drops into the midfield line of 4/5.
tip: The base option.

name: Tracking Wide Midfielder
desc: Tracks back and defends the flank intensely.
tip: Low block.
moveNote: tracks the opposing full-back all the way back

name: Wide Outlet Wide Midfielder
desc: Stays high and wide to launch counter-attacks.
tip: Max. 2 outlets per tactic.
moveNote: stays high and wide for the outlet

name: Free Role
desc: Total freedom to roam and create (replaces Trequartista/Enganche).
tip: Only for your best technical player; give him structure around him.
moveNote: drifts to the ball side

name: Second Striker
desc: Pushes up alongside the striker as a goal threat.
tip: Pair him with a DLF/TF/F9 who drops.
moveNote: joins the striker in the box

name: Attacking Midfielder
desc: Contributes defensively in the opponent’s half.
tip: The base option.

name: Central Outlet Attacking Midfielder
desc: Stays high and central as a counter-attacking target, without defending.
tip: Useful in a low block with Counter-Attack.
moveNote: stays high and central for the outlet

name: Splitting Outlet Attacking Midfielder
desc: Stays high and drifts into the channels to start quick transitions.
tip: Against attacking full-backs.
moveNote: stays high, drifting into the channel

name: Tracking Attacking Midfielder
desc: Tracks back to defend actively, high defensive responsibility.
tip: Low block 4-5-1.
moveNote: drops back to defend

name: Inside Forward
desc: Cuts inside towards goal — a goal threat.
tip: The full-back/wing-back on the same side should give width.
moveNote: cuts inside towards goal

name: Wide Forward
desc: Stays wide but attacks goal (short diagonals, far post).
tip: With an IWB/IFB behind, the flank is well balanced.
moveNote: stays wide and attacks the far post

name: Winger
desc: Standard defending for a winger.
tip: The base option.

name: Tracking Winger
desc: Tracks the opposing full-back all the way back.
tip: Mid/low block with 4-5-1.
moveNote: tracks back

name: Wide Outlet Winger
desc: Stays high and wide for the counter-attack.
tip: Max. 2 outlets.
moveNote: stays wide waiting for the counter

name: Inside Outlet Winger
desc: Stays high and inside, ready to attack the central space in transition.
tip: Pairs with Counter-Attack.
moveNote: stays high and inside

name: Centre Forward
desc: Complete forward: a goal threat who also joins in the build-up.
tip: A safe choice in almost any system.
moveNote: pins the centre-backs and finishes

name: Channel Forward
desc: Attacks the channels between centre-back and full-back.
tip: Opens central space for the AM/SS.
moveNote: attacks the channel

name: Deep-Lying Forward
desc: Drops into the space between the lines and links play.
tip: Needs someone attacking depth (IF, CHM, SS).
moveNote: drops to link play

name: False Nine
desc: Drops into the attacking-midfield zone, drags centre-backs out and creates.
tip: Without runners (IF/CHM/SS) the box stays empty.
moveNote: drops into midfield and drags centre-backs out

name: Poacher
desc: Plays on the last line and lives to finish.
tip: Needs suppliers — creators/crossers.
moveNote: lives on the last line waiting for the ball

name: Target Forward
desc: Target on the last line: wins aerial duels and holds the ball up.
tip: Pair with crosses and "Bypass Press".
moveNote: aerial target in the box

name: Centre Forward
desc: Standard defensive behaviour for a striker.
tip: The base option.

name: Central Outlet Centre Forward
desc: Stays high and central as an outlet.
tip: Low block with Counter-Attack.
moveNote: acts as an outlet

name: Splitting Outlet Centre Forward
desc: Stays high and drifts into the channels waiting for the long ball.
tip: Against defences with very advanced full-backs.
moveNote: stays high, drifting into the channel

name: Tracking Centre Forward
desc: Tracks back to help the defence / is the first to press.
tip: Gegenpress or a compact block.
moveNote: drops and presses the opposing midfielder
